newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Army transfers commander of Aberdeen school.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Army transfers commander of Aberdeen school.

text.p: The U.S. Army announced on Wednesday it was transferring the commander of scandal-plagued Aberdeen Proving Ground training school but denied it had anything to do with a sexual harassment scandal at Aberdeen.

Maj. Gen. Robert Shadley, who has headed the Ordnance Centre and School at the big Aberdeen base in Maryland for two years, will be reassigned to the headquarters of Army Forces Command at Fort McPherson, Georgia, where he will become director of logistics. His replacement at Aberdeen will be Brig. Gen. Thomas Dickinson, currently head of the 13th Corps Support Command at Fort Hood, Texas.

Lt. Col. Bill Harkey, an Army spokesman at the Pentagon, said the reassignment of Shadley, 56, was routine after two years and had nothing to do with charges and convictions for sexual harassment and rape of female recruits by male drill sergeants at Aberdeen. The scandal has also hit other bases.

The Army on Tuesday announced the retirement of the overall commander of the Aberdeen base, Maj. Gen. John Longhouser, who admitted an adulterous affair years ago. But Harkey told Reuters the Shadley transfer "has nothing to do with Longhauser or the issues at Aberdeen. This is just a normal rotation."

The Pentagon has not determined whether lack of supervision by military and civilian leaders created a lax atmosphere at Aberdeen, where 12 Ordnance Centre and School trainers have been charged with preying on female recruits.
The Army and other U.S. military services have been hit hard recently by cases of sexual harassment and marital cheating, which have led to the removal or resignation of a number of senior officers.

"We have very high standards that we insist upon for the military ... It's another example of someone who failed to measure up to those standards," Defence Secretary William Cohen said on Tuesday at a joint news conference with visiting British Defence Secretary George Robertson.

Of the 12 Ordnance Centre and School trainers charged in a sexual misconduct investigation disclosed last November, four were found guilty of violations, two received discharges in lieu of court-martial and six are awaiting resolution.
